import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
import json

np.random.seed(42)

# Sigmoid params from t10_predictions_locked.json
k_mle, k_se = 200.0, 14.2031
ac_mle, ac_se = 0.4755, 0.0018
ym_mle, ym_se = 0.7518, 0.0016

# Bootstrap CIs
k_ci = [73.6101, 499.9488]
ac_ci = [0.425265, 0.557708]
ym_ci = [0.691240, 0.894626]

# Generate bootstrap samples using normal approximation truncated to CI
N = 10000
k_samples = np.clip(np.random.normal(k_mle, k_se, N), k_ci[0], k_ci[1])
ac_samples = np.clip(np.random.normal(ac_mle, ac_se, N), ac_ci[0], ac_ci[1])
ym_samples = np.clip(np.random.normal(ym_mle, ym_se, N), ym_ci[0], ym_ci[1])

# ============ Statistic 1: Δα transition width ============
# Δα = 2*ln(9)/k (sigmoid 10% to 90% width)
delta_alpha = 2 * np.log(9) / k_samples
da_median = np.median(delta_alpha)
da_ci = np.percentile(delta_alpha, [2.5, 97.5])
da_mean = np.mean(delta_alpha)

print('=== Statistic 1: Δα transition width ===')
print(f'  Δα at k_mle={k_mle}: {2*np.log(9)/k_mle:.5f}')
print(f'  Bootstrap median: {da_median:.5f}')
print(f'  Bootstrap mean:   {da_mean:.5f}')
print(f'  Bootstrap 95% CI: [{da_ci[0]:.5f}, {da_ci[1]:.5f}]')
print(f'  Note: even at widest CI (k=73.6), Δα={2*np.log(9)/73.6:.4f}')
print()

# ============ Statistic 2: Δp(0.50 vs 0.45) ============
def sigmoid_rate(alpha, k, ac, ym):
    return ym / (1 + np.exp(-k * (alpha - ac)))

rate_050 = sigmoid_rate(0.50, k_samples, ac_samples, ym_samples)
rate_045 = sigmoid_rate(0.45, k_samples, ac_samples, ym_samples)
delta_p = rate_050 - rate_045

dp_median = np.median(delta_p)
dp_ci = np.percentile(delta_p, [2.5, 97.5])
dp_frac_positive = np.mean(delta_p > 0)

print('=== Statistic 2: Δp(0.50 vs 0.45) ===')
print(f'  At MLE: rate(0.50)={sigmoid_rate(0.50, k_mle, ac_mle, ym_mle):.4f}, rate(0.45)={sigmoid_rate(0.45, k_mle, ac_mle, ym_mle):.4f}')
print(f'  Δp at MLE: {sigmoid_rate(0.50, k_mle, ac_mle, ym_mle) - sigmoid_rate(0.45, k_mle, ac_mle, ym_mle):.4f}')
print(f'  Bootstrap median Δp: {dp_median:.4f}')
print(f'  Bootstrap 95% CI:   [{dp_ci[0]:.4f}, {dp_ci[1]:.4f}]')
print(f'  Fraction Δp > 0:    {dp_frac_positive:.4f}')
print(f'  Fraction Δp > 0.5:  {np.mean(delta_p > 0.5):.4f}')
print()

# But the normal approx for k has SE=14.2 which is very tight
# The REAL bootstrap had k CI [73.6, 500] which is MUCH wider
# Let me also do it with a broader distribution matching actual bootstrap CI
print('--- With broader distribution matching actual bootstrap CI ---')
# Use log-normal for k to match the wide, right-skewed CI
# Fit log-normal: median at ~200, 2.5%ile at 73.6, 97.5%ile at 500
# log(k) ~ N(mu, sigma), median = exp(mu), so mu = log(200) = 5.298
# 2.5%ile: exp(mu - 1.96*sigma) = 73.6 => mu - 1.96*sigma = log(73.6) = 4.298 => sigma = (5.298-4.298)/1.96 = 0.510
log_k_mu = np.log(200)
log_k_sigma = (np.log(200) - np.log(73.6)) / 1.96
k_samples_wide = np.exp(np.random.normal(log_k_mu, log_k_sigma, N))

# Similarly for ac: CI [0.425, 0.558], MLE 0.4755
# This is roughly symmetric, use normal
ac_sigma_wide = (0.558 - 0.425) / (2*1.96)
ac_samples_wide = np.random.normal(0.4755, ac_sigma_wide, N)

# ym: CI [0.691, 0.895], MLE 0.7518
ym_sigma_wide = (0.895 - 0.691) / (2*1.96)
ym_samples_wide = np.random.normal(0.7518, ym_sigma_wide, N)

# Recompute Δα with wide k
delta_alpha_wide = 2 * np.log(9) / k_samples_wide
print(f'  Δα median: {np.median(delta_alpha_wide):.5f}')
print(f'  Δα 95% CI: [{np.percentile(delta_alpha_wide, 2.5):.5f}, {np.percentile(delta_alpha_wide, 97.5):.5f}]')

# Recompute Δp with wide params
rate_050_w = sigmoid_rate(0.50, k_samples_wide, ac_samples_wide, ym_samples_wide)
rate_045_w = sigmoid_rate(0.45, k_samples_wide, ac_samples_wide, ym_samples_wide)
delta_p_wide = rate_050_w - rate_045_w
print(f'  Δp median: {np.median(delta_p_wide):.4f}')
print(f'  Δp 95% CI: [{np.percentile(delta_p_wide, 2.5):.4f}, {np.percentile(delta_p_wide, 97.5):.4f}]')
print(f'  Fraction Δp > 0: {np.mean(delta_p_wide > 0):.4f}')
print()

# ============ Statistic 3: Fisher exact test ============
# α≤0.45: permg_counts[:8] = [0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0] = 0 successes out of 64
# α≥0.50: permg_counts[8:] = [6,3,6,6] = 21 successes out of 32
# 2x2 table: [[successes_low, failures_low], [successes_high, failures_high]]
# = [[0, 64], [21, 11]]
table = np.array([[0, 64], [21, 11]])
odds_ratio, p_value = stats.fisher_exact(table, alternative='greater')
# alternative='greater' tests if group 2 (α≥0.50) has higher success rate

print('=== Statistic 3: Fisher exact test ===')
print(f'  Table: {table.tolist()}')
print(f'  Group α≤0.45: 0/64 = 0.000')
print(f'  Group α≥0.50: 21/32 = {21/32:.3f}')
print(f'  Odds ratio: {odds_ratio}')
print(f'  p-value (one-sided, greater): {p_value:.2e}')
print()

# Also chi-square for comparison
chi2, p_chi2, dof, expected = stats.chi2_contingency(table, correction=True)
print(f'  Chi-square (Yates): χ²={chi2:.1f}, p={p_chi2:.2e}, dof={dof}')
print()

# ============ Key insight ============
print('=== KEY INSIGHT: α_c uncertainty vs transition width ===')
print(f'  α_c CI width:        {0.558-0.425:.3f} (estimation uncertainty)')
print(f'  Δα transition width: {np.median(delta_alpha_wide):.4f} (actual steepness, wide-bootstrap median)')
print(f'  Δα 95% CI:           [{np.percentile(delta_alpha_wide, 2.5):.4f}, {np.percentile(delta_alpha_wide, 97.5):.4f}]')
print(f'  Ratio:               CI_width/Δα = {0.133/np.median(delta_alpha_wide):.1f}×')
print(f'  Interpretation:      The transition IS sharp (Δα small),')
print(f'                       but we dont know exactly WHERE it is (α_c CI wide)')
print(f'                       These are independent quantities.')
print()
print(f'  Fisher p={p_value:.2e}: The EXISTENCE of a jump is unambiguous')
print(f'  Δα CI:               The jump is genuinely steep')
print(f'  α_c CI:              But its exact location has ~0.13 uncertainty')
"
